# Configuration surface

<!-- type: reference · level: 2 -->

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/gen-config-surface.py from `nros knob list --json`. Do not edit by hand.
     Regenerate: python3 scripts/gen-config-surface.py (needs this checkout's nros built)
     Gated by:   just check config-surface -->

Every knob a project can state, with the one place to state it, the
values it takes and its default. A knob is set in the image's
`system.toml`, under `[image.<id>.knobs.<group>]`; a board-scoped knob
can also be set in a board's `nros-board.toml`. `nros knob list` prints
this list for your workspace, including the knobs of packages it
depends on, and `nros knob show <knob>` prints one entry.

A knob has other spellings inside the build, such as an environment
variable or a Kconfig symbol. Those carry the value between build
layers. They are not places to set it, so this page does not list them.

118 knobs in 19 groups.

## `action`

Knobs for action servers and clients.

| Knob | Scope | Default | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`action.inbox_bytes`](#actioninbox_bytes) | image | `-1` | Action inbox slot size (bytes, -1 = derive) |
| [`action.inbox_depth`](#actioninbox_depth) | image | `4` | Action inbox ring depth |

### `action.inbox_bytes`

Action inbox slot size (bytes, -1 = derive)

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.action] inbox_bytes`
- **Scope:** image
- **Values:** an integer
- **Default:** `-1`

Bytes one request slot holds in the inbox ring of each action server
queryable (send_goal, cancel_goal, get_result).

-1 means DERIVE it from this image's declared
`pkg/action/Name_SendGoal_Request` types -- the largest of the three
requests those queryables receive. A SEPARATE family from the service
one above, so neither inherits the other's worst case. Any other value
is yours and WINS; when nothing derives, the crate falls through to
the service family's resolved size. Maps to `action.inbox_bytes`.

### `action.inbox_depth`

Action inbox ring depth

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.action] inbox_depth`
- **Scope:** image
- **Values:** an integer
- **Default:** `4`

Requests one action server queryable holds before the newest is
dropped: the family depth 4 was designed for, and the twin of the C
shim's ZPICO_MAX_PENDING_REPLIES (both 4). Must be >= 1. Maps to
`action.inbox_depth`.

## `clock`

Knobs for the wall clock and its sources.

| Knob | Scope | Default | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`clock.epoch_failure`](#clockepoch_failure) | image | `unstamped` | What boot does when no wall-clock source answers |
| [`clock.fallback_settle_ms`](#clockfallback_settle_ms) | image | `10000` | How long boot waits for each wall-clock source (ms) |
| [`clock.hlc_interval_ms`](#clockhlc_interval_ms) | image | `1000` | Re-take the epoch from zenoh sample timestamps every (ms) |
| [`clock.sntp_attempts`](#clocksntp_attempts) | image | `3` | SNTP queries per boot before the source gives up |
| [`clock.sntp_resync_interval_ms`](#clocksntp_resync_interval_ms) | image | `0` | Re-query the SNTP server every (ms), 0 for once at boot |
| [`clock.sntp_resync_stack_bytes`](#clocksntp_resync_stack_bytes) | image | `8192` | Stack of the SNTP re-sync thread (bytes) |
| [`clock.source`](#clocksource) | image | `platform` | Wall-clock source, or an ordered fallback list |
| [`clock.upgrade`](#clockupgrade) | image | `never` | Whether a better source may replace the latched one later |

### `clock.epoch_failure`

What boot does when no wall-clock source answers

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.clock] epoch_failure`
- **Scope:** image
- **Values:** one of: unstamped, halt
- **Default:** `unstamped`

What the image does when every source in clock.source has been tried and
none answered. `unstamped` boots on: the platform reports no wall clock and
every stamp reads 0, ROS's "unset" time, knowingly. `halt` stops at boot,
for an image whose peers refuse a stamp that is not absolute. A list ending
in `platform` reaches this policy on a port with no clock of its own
(Zephyr, bare-metal FreeRTOS, ThreadX), because `platform` does not answer
there.

### `clock.fallback_settle_ms`

How long boot waits for each wall-clock source (ms)

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.clock] fallback_settle_ms`
- **Scope:** image
- **Values:** an integer from 0 to 600000
- **Default:** `10000`

How long boot waits for each source in clock.source to answer before
trying the next one. 0 tries each once without waiting.

This wait is paid at boot, before the first spin: nothing runs until the
clock is resolved. A zenoh-hlc source that hears no timestamped sample (no
host publishing on a topic the image subscribes to) costs the whole of it
before the next source is tried; an sntp source with no reachable server
costs sntp_attempts x sntp.timeout_ms instead. Timers start counting when
the wait ends, so it is never reported as a missed period.

A board source is asked every 10 ms within it. On a port that resolves on
its first wall-clock read (POSIX, FreeRTOS), that read waits instead of boot.

### `clock.hlc_interval_ms`

Re-take the epoch from zenoh sample timestamps every (ms)

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.clock] hlc_interval_ms`
- **Scope:** image
- **Values:** an integer from 10 to 3600000
- **Default:** `1000`

For the zenoh-hlc source: the window over which the least-delayed
timestamped sample is kept before its offset replaces the installed one.
Shorter tracks a drifting tick more closely; longer is more likely to hold
one low-latency sample.

### `clock.sntp_attempts`

SNTP queries per boot before the source gives up

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.clock] sntp_attempts`
- **Scope:** image
- **Values:** an integer from 1 to 100
- **Default:** `3`

For the sntp source: how many queries boot sends, each waiting up to
sntp.timeout_ms, before the source counts as not answering.

### `clock.sntp_resync_interval_ms`

Re-query the SNTP server every (ms), 0 for once at boot

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.clock] sntp_resync_interval_ms`
- **Scope:** image
- **Values:** an integer from 0 to 86400000
- **Default:** `0`

For the sntp source: above 0, the image queries sntp.server again on this
interval and re-installs the wall-clock offset, so stamps follow a server
whose time steps or a tick that drifts. 0 queries once, at boot. A query
that fails keeps the installed offset. The re-query runs on its own thread
(sized by clock.sntp_resync_stack_bytes) and only while sntp is a source the
image's clock policy admits.

The interval is measured on the image's own monotonic clock. On hardware
that is real time; on a simulator it is GUEST time, so a simulator that runs
faster than real time (an FVP fast-forwarding through idle time, for one)
re-queries correspondingly more often in real time, and one that runs slower
less often.

### `clock.sntp_resync_stack_bytes`

Stack of the SNTP re-sync thread (bytes)

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.clock] sntp_resync_stack_bytes`
- **Scope:** image
- **Values:** an integer from 1024 to 1048576
- **Default:** `8192`

Bytes of stack for the thread clock.sntp_resync_interval_ms starts. It runs
Zephyr's SNTP query (socket, DNS lookup and the exchange), whose depth is
set by Zephyr's network stack, not by nano-ros. Measured with Zephyr 3.7's
thread analyzer:
- 32-bit (mps2-an385, Cortex-M3): 1,160 B with the server named by hostname
  (DNS lookup included), 888 B with a numeric address.
- 64-bit Arm: 7,024 B in an equivalent re-sync thread of a consumer image,
  where 4,096 B overflowed.
The default, 8,192 B, is the 64-bit peak plus the stack-floor margin (10 %,
7,727 B) rounded up to a power of two, so it holds on both. A 32-bit image
may set it lower, down to its own measured peak plus 10 %. The build's
stack-floor walk checks this stack, and refuses one below a measured floor.
The thread exists only when the interval is above 0, so this costs nothing
otherwise.

### `clock.source`

Wall-clock source, or an ordered fallback list

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.clock] source`
- **Scope:** image
- **Values:** an ordered list of distinct members, comma-separated, at least one, of: platform, sntp, zenoh-hlc, board
- **Default:** `platform`

Where the image takes its wall-clock epoch from: one source, or an ordered
fallback tried at boot, comma-separated (sntp,platform). The first source
that answers is latched.

  platform   the platform's own clock (an RTC, or a host's clock). It
             answers only on a port that has one (a POSIX host); on
             Zephyr, FreeRTOS and ThreadX it never answers, so a list
             that ends in it falls through to clock.epoch_failure
  sntp       an SNTP query to sntp.server
  zenoh-hlc  the timestamps on zenoh samples the image receives
  board      a source the board package provides

It is resolved once at boot, after every component has registered and
before anything spins, so no message is stamped before it; see
clock.fallback_settle_ms for what the wait costs.

### `clock.upgrade`

Whether a better source may replace the latched one later

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.clock] upgrade`
- **Scope:** image
- **Values:** one of: never, monotonic
- **Default:** `never`

`never` keeps the source boot latched. `monotonic` lets a source earlier in
clock.source that answers later replace it, provided the wall clock does
not step backwards.

## `entity`

Knobs for the image's entity demand.

| Knob | Scope | Default | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`entity.max_large_subscribers`](#entitymax_large_subscribers) | image | `-1` | Subscribers served from the large payload class (-1 = derive) |
| [`entity.max_liveliness`](#entitymax_liveliness) | image | `-1` | Maximum concurrent liveliness tokens (-1 = derive) |
| [`entity.max_pending_gets`](#entitymax_pending_gets) | image | `4` | Maximum concurrent pending get operations |
| [`entity.max_publishers`](#entitymax_publishers) | image | `-1` | Maximum concurrent publishers (-1 = derive) |
| [`entity.max_queryables`](#entitymax_queryables) | image | `-1` | Maximum concurrent queryables (-1 = derive) |
| [`entity.max_subscribers`](#entitymax_subscribers) | image | `-1` | Maximum concurrent subscribers (-1 = derive) |

### `entity.max_large_subscribers`

Subscribers served from the large payload class (-1 = derive)

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.entity] max_large_subscribers`
- **Scope:** image
- **Values:** an integer
- **Default:** `-1`

Subscribers whose rx_buffer_hint exceeds SUBSCRIBER_SIZE_THRESHOLD and
are therefore served from LARGE_PAYLOADS. Bounded separately from
entity.max_subscribers so raising SUBSCRIBER_LARGE_SIZE for one
image-scale topic does not multiply across every subscriber. This is the
DEMAND (RMW-agnostic). The zenoh pool, zenoh.max_large_subscribers
(`zenoh.max_large_subscribers`, the C macro
`zenoh.max_large_subscribers`), is derived from it.

-1 means DERIVE it: how many types in the linked interface closure
exceed the class split. Do not count it by reading generated C++
headers BY EYE: they state an ESTIMATE and not a bound, and a count
made that way can give 2 where the derived answer is 0.

0 is a legal, meaningful value and NOT the same as -1: it claims that
every type this image receives fits the small class, and the large pool
becomes zero bytes instead of RING_DEPTH x LARGE_SIZE. A hint no class
can hold is then refused at create_subscription rather than served a
block too small for it.

Derived counts TYPES, not subscriptions -- an upper bound, since the
closure is what is linked, not what is subscribed. See
`subscriber.buffer_bytes` for the rest of that caveat.

### `entity.max_liveliness`

Maximum concurrent liveliness tokens (-1 = derive)

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.entity] max_liveliness`
- **Scope:** image
- **Values:** an integer
- **Default:** `-1`

Maximum number of liveliness tokens this image declares at once.
This is the DEMAND (RMW-agnostic). The zenoh pool, zenoh.max_liveliness
(`zenoh.max_liveliness`, the C macro `zenoh.max_liveliness`), is derived
from it, floored at 1.

`-1` DERIVES this from the image's entity inventory,
on the same ladder as `entity.max_queryables`. Stating a number here WINS.

Every token is declared by THIS session, never by a peer: one for the
session's own node, one per node name, and one per publisher,
subscriber, service server and service client (three per action
client, which the derivation multiplies). The graph cache's own
subscriber takes no slot. An image with no inventory (nothing
declared) keeps the zpico default of 16.

Short is not a boot failure: the entity works and is invisible to
`ros2 node list`, and the shim logs the exhaustion naming this knob.
An image that BRIDGES (runtime-named nodes, declared nowhere) must
state it.

### `entity.max_pending_gets`

Maximum concurrent pending get operations

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.entity] max_pending_gets`
- **Scope:** image
- **Values:** an integer
- **Default:** `4`

Maximum number of concurrent pending get (service call) operations. This
is the DEMAND (RMW-agnostic). The zenoh pool, zenoh.max_pending_gets
(`zenoh.max_pending_gets`, the C macro `zenoh.max_pending_gets`), is
derived from it.

### `entity.max_publishers`

Maximum concurrent publishers (-1 = derive)

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.entity] max_publishers`
- **Scope:** image
- **Values:** an integer
- **Default:** `-1`

Maximum number of publishers this image opens at once.
This is the DEMAND (RMW-agnostic). The zenoh pool, zenoh.max_publishers
(`zenoh.max_publishers`, the C macro `zenoh.max_publishers`), is derived
from it, floored at 1.

`-1` DERIVES this from the image's entity inventory
(`nano_ros_node_register(... ENTITIES ...)`). Stating a number here WINS
and suppresses the derivation, which is a fine thing to do deliberately
and a silent cost otherwise.

The derived value counts what the SESSION opens, which is not what the
author declares: a declared action server is one entity that costs three
queryables and two publishers, and an action client one subscription.
Those multipliers live beside the calls that decide them.

NOT counted, because a feature enables them and the inventory cannot see
it: the parameter (6) and lifecycle (5) service families. An image
carrying either must state this knob.

### `entity.max_queryables`

Maximum concurrent queryables (-1 = derive)

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.entity] max_queryables`
- **Scope:** image
- **Values:** an integer
- **Default:** `-1`

Maximum number of queryables (service servers) this image opens at once.
This is the DEMAND (RMW-agnostic). The zenoh pool, zenoh.max_queryables
(`zenoh.max_queryables`, the C macro `zenoh.max_queryables`), is derived
from it, floored at 1.

`-1` DERIVES this from the image's entity inventory
(`nano_ros_node_register(... ENTITIES ...)`). Stating a number here WINS
and suppresses the derivation, which is a fine thing to do deliberately
and a silent cost otherwise.

The derived value counts what the SESSION opens, which is not what the
author declares: a declared action server is one entity that costs three
queryables and two publishers, and an action client one subscription.
Those multipliers live beside the calls that decide them.

NOT counted, because a feature enables them and the inventory cannot see
it: the parameter (6) and lifecycle (5) service families. An image
carrying either must state this knob.

The PARAMETER family is per NODE. `ros2 param list`
enumerates an image's nodes, so one set of six services is registered
under each node's own fully-qualified name: an N-node image carrying
`[param_services]` claims 6*N slots before the application declares
anything, plus 5 for the lifecycle family, which is still one set on the
executor. A value below that DERIVED floor is refused at BUILD time by
`nros-zpico-build` and the refusal names this knob -- it used to be a
runtime `ServiceServerCreationFailed` with no explanation.
Two nodes already need 12, which is over the historical default of 8.

The derived value counts what the SESSION opens, which is not what the

### `executor.action_clients`

Callback slots to budget at ActionClient size (-1 = derive)

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.executor] action_clients`
- **Or for a board:** `nros-board.toml`, `[knobs] executor.action_clients`
- **Scope:** image
- **Values:** an integer
- **Default:** `-1`

How many of `executor.max_cbs` slots the arena derivation budgets at
ACTION CLIENT size (~18 KiB each) rather than pub/sub size (~3.5 KiB).

-1 DERIVES it from the image's entity inventory, the same way MAX_CBS is
derived: the count is the action clients AND action servers the image's
components declare. An image whose inventory refuses -- any component
that declared no ENTITIES -- falls through to MAX_CBS, which reproduces
the historical arithmetic exactly, so nothing built before this moves.

Action SERVERS count too, though the option is named for clients: the
arena stores ActionServerArenaEntry, so a server image occupies the same
heavy slots and zeroing this on one would trade the saving for a runtime
BufferTooSmall.

Set it to 0 on an image with no action client: at the defaults that takes
the arena from 74240 bytes to 16384. The arena is INLINE ON THE TASK
STACK, not in .bss, so this is stack headroom -- see the FreeRTOS
"Invalid mbox" note in book-internals/src/platform/implementation-notes.md.

Too small fails at REGISTRATION with BufferTooSmall, not at link. The
executor reports what it actually used on its first spin, so build once,
read the advisory, then set this.

### `executor.arena_bytes`

Executor arena size in bytes (0 = derive)

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.executor] arena_bytes`
- **Or for a board:** `nros-board.toml`, `[knobs] executor.arena_bytes`
- **Scope:** image
- **Values:** an integer
- **Default:** `0`

Explicit executor arena size. 0 means let nros-node build.rs derive it,
which budgets EVERY callback slot at action-client size (~18 KiB) --
correct, but several times over for a pub/sub-only image, which needs
about max_cbs * ((depth + 1) * (`executor.subscription_buffer_bytes` + 8) + 1024)
+ 2048.

MIND THE DEPTH. A subscription's arena claim scales with its
QoS history: KEEP_LAST(N > 1) is a ring of N + 1 slots plus a length
beside each, and the ROS default is KEEP_LAST(10), so one ordinary
subscription at the default buffer size costs 12 KiB and not 3.5 KiB.
This help said "3 * `executor.subscription_buffer_bytes` + 512" until the
derivation itself did, and an image sized from that arithmetic dies at
entity creation with NodeError::BufferTooSmall.

Set it only with that arithmetic in hand. On an image that DECLARES its
entities (every NROS_ENTITY_COUNT_* reached the build), a value below
what they are modelled to need does not build: nros-node refuses it at
compile time, naming this option, both numbers and the shortfall
(executor::arena_oracle). On an image that declares nothing
the derivation is a worst-case budget, not a requirement, so a smaller
value is accepted -- and too small still fails at runtime, at the first
registration that does not fit, not at link.

### `executor.backing_bytes`

Executor backing reservation in 64-bit words (-1 = derive, 0 = none)

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.executor] backing_bytes`
- **Or for a board:** `nros-board.toml`, `[knobs] executor.backing_bytes`
- **Scope:** image
- **Values:** an integer
- **Default:** `-1`

How many 64-bit words nros-node reserves in .bss for the executor's
per-entry storage -- the named static
nros_node::executor::backing::EXECUTOR_BACKING. The reservation is
exactly 8 x this many bytes, on every target.

-1 DERIVES it, from ExecutorSizing::DEFAULT: MAX_CBS, MAX_SC, MAX_NODES
and the arena (and the parameter store, when the image builds one).

A STATED number covers the executor's tables only: when the image builds
a parameter store (NROS_CAPABILITY_PARAM_SERVICES or NROS_PARAMS_STORE),
the store's words are carved from the same static and added ON TOP, so
the reservation is then 8 x (this + the store). Deriving is the right
answer for an image that does not care which budget the bytes come out
of.

STATE A NUMBER when the image lowers CONFIG_COMMON_LIBC_MALLOC_ARENA_SIZE
to pay for the reservation. The Rust global allocator here is picolibc
malloc, whose arena is ITSELF a fixed static, and the backing used to be
a Box::leak out of it -- so leaving that arena where it was reserves the
same bytes twice. Lowering it by a number copied out of `nm` pairs them
once and then drifts the next time an executor knob moves, in whichever
direction, with nothing to say so.

Stating the size inverts that. The crate obeys this number, so the
pairing is exact by construction and identical on every board -- the
DERIVED size is target-dependent (87,256 B on mps2_an385 against
88,328 B on native_sim/native/64 for one and the same conf, which is how
a conf hand-paired on one board kept double-reserving 1,072 bytes on the
other) and 8 x this is not. State it too SMALL and nros-node refuses to
compile naming this knob, which is the direction that would otherwise
silently re-create the double reservation.

THE PAIRING ABOVE IS RETIRED. Every Zephyr Rust allocation now goes to
the nros heap (`memory.heap_bytes`), so no Rust byte
reaches picolibc's arena and there is nothing in it to lower; the six
example confs that did so (a `# nros-arena-base:` marker, this knob and
a lowered COMMON_LIBC_MALLOC_ARENA_SIZE) state none of the three now,
and check-executor-backing-arena-pairing refuses the marker. Stating
this knob is still how an image fixes the reservation at 8 x N bytes on
every board. That a value is stated does not make it ENOUGH: the executor
grows, the conf does not, and the image stops compiling. `just check
node-std-tests` checks every stated value against the MEASURED default
on each board the conf is built for, so restate it there.

0 declines the static entirely and restores the old Box::leak, for an
image that would rather keep the bytes in the allocator arena than have
the linker price them.

### `executor.extra_sessions`

Extra-session slots per executor (-1 = derive)

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.executor] extra_sessions`
- **Scope:** image
- **Values:** an integer
- **Default:** `-1`

Slots for sessions a node opens on an RMW backend other
than the primary's (NodeBuilder::rmw, open_multi), per executor (per
sched_task), at most one per node slot. A slot is the backend's session
(528 bytes on thumbv7em with zenoh) plus a 168-byte id.

`-1` derives it from the image's backend count (the sizing
descriptor's [image] backend_count, which also sizes the RMW backend
registry): backends - 1, so 0 for a one-RMW image. With no backend
count stated, one per node slot (the old size). State a count only for
a second session on the SAME backend (another locator or domain, on a
backend that allows it); a full table is NodeError::NodeTableFull.

### `executor.max_age_monitors`

Contract-monitor age rows per executor (-1 = derive)

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.executor] max_age_monitors`
- **Scope:** image
- **Values:** an integer
- **Default:** `-1`

Age contract rows one executor watches (nros-node build.rs
MAX_AGE_MONITORS): one per contracted subscription
carrying max_age_ms. A separate knob from `executor.max_monitors`
because it is a separate table, so an image with rate contracts and
no age contracts pays for one table only. `-1` derives it on the same
terms, and a longer table is refused naming this knob.

### `executor.max_cbs`

Maximum executor callback slots (-1 = derive)

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.executor] max_cbs`
- **Or for a board:** `nros-board.toml`, `[knobs] executor.max_cbs`
- **Scope:** image
- **Values:** an integer
- **Default:** `-1`

Maximum number of callback slots in the executor
(subscriptions + timers + services + service clients + action
entities + guard conditions). Controls both Rust and C APIs.
Arena size is derived automatically from this value and the
subscription buffer size.

A PUBLISHER IS NOT ONE OF THEM. Every registration that claims a slot
calls Executor::next_entry_slot(); create_publisher does not — it writes
an RmwPublisher into caller-owned storage and there is no
nros_executor_add_publisher on the C path. For example, an image with
19 slot-claiming entities and 14 publishers needs 19 here, not 33.

-1 means DERIVE it from this image's ENTITY inventory: the sum of every
`nano_ros_node_register(... ENTITIES ...)` declaration in the image,
counted by kind. It is derived only when EVERY component declared; one
that did not makes the whole image refuse, so a partial answer can never
be published as a whole one. Any value other than -1 is yours and WINS;
the crate default when nothing is stated and nothing is derivable is 4.

The derived value carries NO headroom, which makes the running image a
checker of its own declaration: one entity past the table and
registration returns ExecutorFull naming this knob, and the entry halts
boot naming the node. Raise it deliberately if you want slack — the
arena scales with it.

4 is the crate default in nros-node/build.rs. Zephyr C images once
compiled that default whatever was configured here, because this option
did not reach Cargo; the old Kconfig default of 16 had therefore never
been built, and honouring it would have grown a native_sim listener's
.bss by 219 KB (+35%).

### `executor.max_monitors`

Contract-monitor rate/latency rows per executor (-1 = derive)

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.executor] max_monitors`
- **Scope:** image
- **Values:** an integer
- **Default:** `-1`

Rate/latency contract rows one executor watches (nros-node build.rs
MAX_MONITORS). One row per contracted
publisher carrying min_rate_hz, plus latency-only rows from node
paths carrying max_latency_ms.

`-1` DERIVES this from the image's entity inventory, which counts the
rows from the same contract the entry bakes its table from. Without
a contract the crate default of 8 stands. A stated number wins, in
both directions. The rows are inline in the executor (24 bytes each
on a 32-bit target), so a board file should never state a count the
contract already determines. A table longer than this is REFUSED at
install (nros_cpp_install_monitors logs this knob's name and returns
NROS_CPP_RET_FULL; a Rust entry fails to compile), never truncated.

### `executor.max_nodes`

Maximum nodes per executor (-1 = derive)

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.executor] max_nodes`
- **Or for a board:** `nros-board.toml`, `[knobs] executor.max_nodes`
- **Scope:** image
- **Values:** an integer
- **Default:** `-1`

Nodes attachable to one executor (nros-node build.rs MAX_NODES).

### `executor.max_sc`

Maximum scheduling-context slots per executor (-1 = derive)

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.executor] max_sc`
- **Or for a board:** `nros-board.toml`, `[knobs] executor.max_sc`
- **Scope:** image
- **Values:** an integer
- **Default:** `-1`

SchedContext slots per executor (nros-node build.rs MAX_SC).

`-1` DERIVES this from the image's entity inventory:
slot 0 is the reserved default Fifo context (create_sched_context
searches 1..MAX_SC), plus one per scheduling context the schedule can
create. The Rust runtime creates NONE -- apply_sched_task_sched_policy ends
in set_default_sched_context, which mutates slot 0 -- while the C/C++
entry pack creates one per sched_task. A stated number wins, in both
directions. The old default was 8 for every image whatever it
declared, worth 112 bytes a slot in the executor backing on
thumbv7m-none-eabi. Too small is NodeError::NoSchedContextSlot at
create_sched_context, which names this knob.

### `executor.max_shutdown_cbs`

Shutdown-hook slots per phase

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.executor] max_shutdown_cbs`
- **Or for a board:** `nros-board.toml`, `[knobs] executor.max_shutdown_cbs`
- **Scope:** image
- **Values:** an integer
- **Default:** `2`

How many shutdown hooks the executor can hold PER PHASE — one table
this size for pre-shutdown hooks (run while the session is still open,
so a node can publish a final state or park an actuator) and a second
for on-shutdown hooks (run after the close). Read by nros-node/build.rs
as `executor.max_shutdown_cbs`.

Deliberately small: the slots are static, so every image pays for them
whether or not it registers a hook, as queryable slots do. Raise it only
when an image genuinely has more things to park on the way down.
Overflow is reported at registration (RCLC_RET_FULL), not silently
dropped.

### `executor.max_violations`

Contract-violation ring depth per executor

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.executor] max_violations`
- **Scope:** image
- **Values:** an integer from 1 to 256
- **Default:** `8`

How many contract violations one executor's ring
keeps for a drain (nros-node build.rs MAX_VIOLATIONS), and the slot
count of the image-wide SWD record NROS_VIOLATION_RECORD (present
with CONFIG_NROS_BOOT_REPORT).

The ring keeps the LATEST entries: a violation into a full ring
evicts the oldest and counts it (Executor::violations_dropped). It
used to keep the FIRST entries, so a board whose start-up filled it
stored nothing after. A slot costs 24 bytes in the ring and 28 in the
record on a 32-bit target; 8 is 192 B per executor plus 264 B for
the record. Raise it only when a burst must be kept whole.

### `executor.param_service_buffer_bytes`

Parameter service request/reply buffer size (bytes) (-1 = derive)

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.executor] param_service_buffer_bytes`
- **Or for a board:** `nros-board.toml`, `[knobs] executor.param_service_buffer_bytes`
- **Scope:** image
- **Values:** an integer
- **Default:** `-1`

Each half of the one request/reply buffer pair an executor's
parameter services share (nros-node build.rs PARAM_SERVICE_BUFFER_SIZE).

-1 DERIVES it: when the contract's `params:` declare
every node's parameters, nros-node sizes the buffer for the largest
message those names and types can produce at the store's capacities
(`params.max_string_value_bytes`, `params.max_array_len`,
`params.max_byte_array_bytes`, `params.max_description_bytes`).
Without a declaration the crate default of 4096 stands. Stating a
number here WINS; a request or reply past it is dropped and logged
once per service.

### `executor.runtime_remaps`

Runtime remap-table slots per executor (-1 = derive)

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.executor] runtime_remaps`
- **Scope:** image
- **Values:** an integer
- **Default:** `-1`

Slots of one executor's RUNTIME remap
table (nros-node build.rs RUNTIME_REMAPS): `--ros-args -r` rules and
rules hand-written code declares with nros_cpp_declare_remap /
Executor::declare_remap. The launch file's <remap> rules are NOT here:
the generated entry emits them as one const table in flash that every
executor reads (nros_cpp_set_launch_remaps).

`-1` derives it: 16 on a target with process arguments (Linux, NuttX),
0 on bare metal (Zephyr, FreeRTOS, ThreadX), which has no argv. A rule
costs 404 bytes on a 32-bit target, per executor (per sched_task). At 0,
declare_remap is refused by name (RemapRefused::NoRuntimeTable,
NROS_CPP_RET_FULL); state a count here to restore runtime slots.

### `executor.subscription_buffer_bytes`

Per-subscription receive buffer size in bytes (-1 = derive)

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.executor] subscription_buffer_bytes`
- **Or for a board:** `nros-board.toml`, `[knobs] executor.subscription_buffer_bytes`
- **Scope:** image
- **Values:** an integer
- **Default:** `-1`

Serialized-sample capacity of every executor arena subscription
(nros-node build.rs DEFAULT_RX_BUF_SIZE). A sample larger than this
is dropped at take with BUFFER_TOO_SMALL — for the C++ arena
dispatch path that drop is silent, so an undersized buffer looks
like a subscription that never fires. Size it to the largest
serialized message the image subscribes to (e.g. an Autoware
/planning trajectory runs 9-14 KiB). The executor arena is derived
from this value times the callback-slot count — raise it
deliberately.

-1 means DERIVE it from this image's message-bound inventory: the
largest derived bound in the LINKED interface closure, which is an UPPER
BOUND on what the image needs and never an under-estimate. "Size it to
the largest serialized message the image subscribes to" is exactly the
instruction nobody could follow by hand -- for example, a board conf can
reason its way to ~718 B for nav_msgs/Odometry and write 512, where the
derived bound is 880. Any value other than -1 is yours and WINS; the
crate default when nothing is stated and nothing is derivable is 1024.

COUPLED TO THE ARENA: each subscription's receive region holds
(depth + 1) x (this + 8) bytes at a KEEP_LAST depth above 1, the ROS
default being 10 (3 x this at depth 1), and an image that declares no
entities budgets every callback slot at action-client size, which also
grows by 3 x this. So raising this raises the arena; `executor.arena_bytes`
gives the whole arithmetic. An image that also PINS
`executor.arena_bytes` must move the two together; leaving both to
derive is the shape that cannot disagree.

## `freertos`

| Knob | Scope | Default | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`freertos.task_stack_guard`](#freertostask_stack_guard) | board | chosen by the build | 0 builds a FreeRTOS kernel that does not reprogram the board's task stack |

### `freertos.task_stack_guard`

0 builds a FreeRTOS kernel that does not reprogram the board's task stack

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.freertos] task_stack_guard`
- **Scope:** board
- **Package:** `nros_platform_freertos`
- **Values:** an integer (not checked before the build)
- **Default:** chosen by the build

0 builds a FreeRTOS kernel that does not reprogram the board's task stack
guard on a context switch, so a task that overflows its stack is no longer
stopped by the MPU. 1 keeps the guard. Unset keeps the board's own default:
on for a board that has a guard (MPS2-AN385 guards the lowest 256 bytes of
each task stack), off for one that does not.

## `log`

Knobs for logging.

| Knob | Scope | Default | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`log.buffer_bytes`](#logbuffer_bytes) | image | `256` | nros-log per-call formatting buffer (bytes) |
| [`log.dynamic_loggers`](#logdynamic_loggers) | image | `16` | Loggers nros-log may create at run time |
| [`log.early_records`](#logearly_records) | image | `4` | nros-log records held for delivery |
| [`log.max_level`](#logmax_level) | image | `0` | nros-log compile-time severity ceiling |
| [`log.rosout_records`](#logrosout_records) | image | `16` | nros-log /rosout queue depth |

### `log.buffer_bytes`

nros-log per-call formatting buffer (bytes)

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.log] buffer_bytes`
- **Or for a board:** `nros-board.toml`, `[knobs] log.buffer_bytes`
- **Scope:** image
- **Values:** an integer from 128 to 4096
- **Default:** `256`

Bytes of the buffer one Rust log call formats into, and of the message
held in each early-record and /rosout slot (nros-log build.rs, as
`log.buffer_bytes`). Longer messages are truncated with
an ellipsis. The C/C++ NROS_LOG_* printf front-end keeps its own
256-byte frame (<rclc/log.h>), so a C record is bounded by the smaller
of the two. Bigger costs stack on every logging task. Replaces the
deprecated buffer-size-<N> cargo features.

### `log.dynamic_loggers`

Loggers nros-log may create at run time

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.log] dynamic_loggers`
- **Or for a board:** `nros-board.toml`, `[knobs] log.dynamic_loggers`
- **Scope:** image
- **Values:** an integer from 0 to 1024
- **Default:** `16`

How many loggers nros_log::get_or_create_logger may CREATE at run time
(nros-log build.rs, as `log.dynamic_loggers`): a node's own logger,
every distinct get_logger("x") and every distinct child name each take
one slot. Each slot costs a Logger plus 24 bytes of name arena in .bss.

0 declines the arenas entirely -- no runtime loggers, lookup only --
which is right for an image whose loggers are all static. A creation
past the capacity falls back to the parent logger and warns once.

Size it from a measurement: the boot report records the slots in use
against this capacity, and a static-memory report of the image prices
the arenas.
A board states its own default in [knobs.log] dynamic_loggers;
this Kconfig value outranks it, and the environment outranks both.

### `log.early_records`

nros-log records held for delivery

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.log] early_records`
- **Or for a board:** `nros-board.toml`, `[knobs] log.early_records`
- **Scope:** image
- **Values:** an integer from 0 to 256
- **Default:** `4`

How many records nros_log::early holds until a sink can take them:
before init installs the sinks, or while another thread is inside a
sink. nros-log build.rs reads it as
`log.early_records`. 0 declines the queue: such
records are dropped and only counted, and the count is logged.
Each slot is a formatting buffer plus a logger name in .bss.
Replaces the deprecated early-records-<N> cargo features.

### `log.max_level`

nros-log compile-time severity ceiling

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.log] max_level`
- **Or for a board:** `nros-board.toml`, `[knobs] log.max_level`
- **Scope:** image
- **Values:** an integer from 0 to 6, or one of: trace, debug, info, warn, error, fatal, off
- **Default:** `0`

The least severe record the image can emit at all (nros-log build.rs,
as `log.max_level`): 0 trace, 1 debug, 2 info, 3 warn,
4 error, 5 fatal, 6 off. A number, as Zephyr's own LOG_MAX_LEVEL is.

Rust nros_*! call sites below the ceiling compile to nothing; C and
C++ records below it are refused at the facade (the same check
nros_log_is_enabled answers). It is a BOUND, not the runtime level:
rclc_logger_set_level / set_level still move each logger's threshold
beneath it. Replaces the retired max-level-* cargo features.

### `log.rosout_records`

nros-log /rosout queue depth

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.log] rosout_records`
- **Or for a board:** `nros-board.toml`, `[knobs] log.rosout_records`
- **Scope:** image
- **Values:** an integer from 1 to 1024
- **Default:** `16`

Records the /rosout queue holds between pumps, and the KEEP_LAST
depth of the /rosout publisher (nros-log build.rs, as
`log.rosout_records`). Only paid when nros-node's
rosout feature is on. Replaces the deprecated rosout-records-<N>
cargo features.

## `memory`

Knobs for stacks and heaps, per image.

| Knob | Scope | Default | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`memory.app_stack_bytes`](#memoryapp_stack_bytes) | board | per platform | Bytes of the application task's stack: the task that runs registration, |
| [`memory.heap_bytes`](#memoryheap_bytes) | board | `65536` (varies) | Application heap arena size (bytes) |

### `memory.app_stack_bytes`

Bytes of the application task's stack: the task that runs registration,

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.memory] app_stack_bytes`
- **Or for a board:** `nros-board.toml`, `[knobs] memory.app_stack_bytes`
- **Scope:** board
- **Values:** an integer of 0 or more
- **Default:** set per platform and board; `nros knob list --platform <p>` shows the value one platform gets, and which rung set it

Bytes of the application task's stack: the task that runs registration,
Executor::open and the spin loop. One knob on every platform that sizes
it (FreeRTOS, ThreadX, and bare-metal mps2-an385, where the application
runs on the main stack); each platform's build converts it to the unit its
RTOS configuration takes, in the one place that writes that
configuration. Unset, the board's own default applies (FreeRTOS: 128 KiB
on the cargo road, 64 KiB on the cmake road; ThreadX rv-virt: 512 KiB;
mps2-an385 bare metal: 256 KiB, a whole number of KiB so the MPU guard
below it stays aligned), raised to the measured stack floor where the
build walks one.

### `memory.heap_bytes`

Application heap arena size (bytes)

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.memory] heap_bytes`
- **Or for a board:** `nros-board.toml`, `[knobs] memory.heap_bytes`
- **Scope:** board
- **Values:** an integer
- **Default:** the first that applies:
  - `1048576` if the image uses Cyclone DDS
  - `-1` if the image has lifecycle nodes (-1: derived from its state machines and nodes)
  - `-1` if the image has parameter services (-1: derived from the nodes serving them)
  - `114688` if the image seeds a parameter store
  - `131072` if the image has Rust code
  - `65536` otherwise

Bytes of the application heap. On FreeRTOS it is heap_4's arena
(configTOTAL_HEAP_SIZE; the board build converts it to the KiB its
FreeRTOSConfig.h takes, and derives it when unset). On Zephyr it is the
nros heap arena, with the defaults below. ThreadX's byte pool is its
own knob, threadx.byte_pool_bytes. On bare metal (mps2-an385, stm32f4)
it is the platform crate's static free-list heap, read at compile time
(defaults 128 KiB and 32 KiB).

A PARAM_SERVICES image, one whose launch seeds a parameter
(NROS_PARAMS_STORE), and a LIFECYCLE one get 192 KiB: those capabilities
allocate their services' buffers from this arena, and nothing sized it
from the declaration, so such an image LINKED and then halted at boot.

The PARAMETER STORE is NOT in this arena any more. Those two symbols are
exactly what makes nros-params carve the store out of the executor's
.bss backing (nros_params::IMPLIED_STORE_SLOTS), so the store's ~8.5 KiB
a slot -- 285,696 bytes at the default 32 slots, the `HEAP EXHAUSTED
(TOO SMALL): request 285696` such an image used to halt with -- moved to
the linker and out of this default. It was 512 KiB for param_services
until 2026-10-09; MEASURED after the move, zephyr_cpp_params (both axes)
boots at 192 KiB, prints `parameter store: 32 slots (285696 B) carved
from the executor backing` and reads its launch-seeded 250 back. A store
only application code reaches is invisible to the build, stays on this
heap, and is refused at run time with its size.

MEASURED on native_sim/native/64 (boot record, live router,
`read-boot-report.py --heap-headroom`), on features' images that
declare BOTH axes: zephyr_cpp_params peaks at 111,360 without the store
(46,848 with param_services alone, so lifecycle costs ~64.5 KiB --
five services, each owning a 2 x 4,096-byte buffer pair); the Rust
params image at 114,144 without it, and the lifecycle and qos images'
peaks less the store at 113,904 and 120,896.
Worst + the 24,576-byte floor is 145,472, hence 192 KiB for LIFECYCLE.

An image with param_services (or a seeded store) and no lifecycle gets
112 KiB, Rust included: the 64 KiB default plus the 46,848-byte
param_services peak above. A Rust image used to get 192 KiB here,
because its 114,144 peak was taken on the both-axes image and not split.
MEASURED split since: features' zephyr_rust_params on
native_sim/native/64, which declares the lifecycle capability but runs no
managed node, peaks at 45,840 B. And 192 KiB is what stopped a stock
Rust action server linking on nucleo_f767zi (384 KiB SRAM): RAM overflowed
by 77,504 B, and the 81,920 B this saves is what fits it. Since the stock node interfaces are on in
every image, 192 KiB there put 128 KiB of unused heap on every
C/C++ zenoh image, and a nucleo_f767zi serial talker no longer fit.
That 46,848 is the ONE-NODE case: zephyr_cpp_params serves the
parameter services on one node. The cost is per NODE, since each of a
node's six parameter services owns a 2 x PARAM_SERVICE_BUFFER_SIZE
buffer pair. So an image serving them on several nodes does not fit
112 KiB: the four-node derived-sched-tasks image ran it dry at boot.
The same holds for the 192 KiB lifecycle arm: a lifecycle state
machine owns five such pairs. So on Zephyr the param_services and
lifecycle arms are the -1 derive sentinel. The configure starts from
the arm the image had (112 KiB for param_services, 192 KiB for
lifecycle) and adds (nodes - 1) x (12 x PARAM_SERVICE_BUFFER_SIZE) and
(machines - 1) x (10 x PARAM_SERVICE_BUFFER_SIZE), each plus a measured
remainder, from the counts in the image's entity inventory
(zephyr/cmake/nros_heap_floor.cmake). One node and one machine derive
exactly the arm; with no inventory to count from, the image keeps the
arm. A value stated here, in the environment, or in the image's
`[image.<id>.knobs.memory] heap_bytes` still wins, and one below the
derived floor is warned about at configure. An image that only seeds a
store, without the services, keeps its flat arm.

A CYCLONE image gets 1 MiB: ddsrt's whole heap lands here
since the Zephyr road compiles the platform funnel (heap/nros/heap.c),
where it used to be picolibc's 16 MiB arena. MEASURED on
native_sim/native/64, c/talker cyclonedds: 840 nros_platform_alloc calls
and a 153,072-byte peak by the first dds_write (gdb); 1 MiB is ~6.8x
that, for discovery and samples in flight a peerless run does not reach.
A Rust Cyclone image's Rust allocations share it.

A RUST application gets twice the default: its Rust
`alloc` goes through this arena too -- it used to land in a second,
unpriced heap (zephyr-lang-rust's CONFIG_RUST_ALLOC over libc malloc).
MEASURED one-heap peaks on native_sim/native/64 (boot record, 10 s
against a live peer): rust/talker xrce 46,256; rust/listener zenoh
42,304; rust/action-server zenoh 58,288 -- which leaves 7,760 bytes of
a 64 KiB arena and is refused by `read-boot-report.py --heap-headroom`.
128 KiB keeps the 24,576-byte floor over the worst of them.

A C or C++ zenoh image keeps 64 KiB. MEASURED peaks (boot
record, 20-40 s against a live peer, Zephyr 3.7): talker 13,472 on
mps2_an385 (C and C++), 11,664 on nucleo_f767zi (serial, Renode twin),
16,544 on native_sim/native/64; and on native_sim, listener 15,984,
service server 16,816, service client 20,496, action server 33,648,
action client 33,568 (C and C++ alike). The action images set the
default: 33,648 + the 24,576-byte floor is 58,224. A C image that
declares no action could take 48 KiB; nothing in Kconfig knows what an
image declares, so that image states it.

Size of the rlsf arena in nros-platform's zephyr_heap, which backs
BOTH z_malloc and __rust_alloc since the allocation funnel moved off
Zephyr's kernel heap.

CONFIG_HEAP_MEM_POOL_SIZE does NOT govern application allocation any
more; this does. An application that outgrows the arena does not
fault or log -- it stops, so size this to what the application
actually needs rather than leaving the default in place and
inferring from a hang.

An `memory.heap_bytes` environment variable overrides this value.

The boot record's capacity word reads this value + 512: zpico-alloc
carves an 8 x 64 B slab beside the arena, so a
configured 102400 reads 102912. Size from a dump with
`read-boot-report.py --heap-headroom`, which judges the RUNNING peak
(as of the dump) against a 24,576-byte floor and names the knob
(peak + floor - 512); take the dump after the host graph has joined,
not at boot.

PERMANENTLY OPERATOR-STATED beyond those defaults. The
arena's peak is a RUNTIME property: it moves with what the peers send
(discovery, the graph, samples in flight), which nothing in the image
declares, so no build can derive it. The defaults above are floors per
declared capability; the measured peak, read off the boot record by
`read-boot-report.py --heap-headroom`, is how an image is sized past
them, and it names the value to state.

## `params`

Knobs for parameters and their services.

| Knob | Scope | Default | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`params.events_depth`](#paramsevents_depth) | image | `1` | /parameter_events publisher history depth |
| [`params.max_array_len`](#paramsmax_array_len) | image | `-1` | Array parameter capacity in elements (-1 = derive) |
| [`params.max_byte_array_bytes`](#paramsmax_byte_array_bytes) | image | `-1` | Byte-array parameter capacity in bytes (-1 = derive) |
| [`params.max_constraints_bytes`](#paramsmax_constraints_bytes) | image | `0` | Parameter additional_constraints capacity in bytes |
| [`params.max_description_bytes`](#paramsmax_description_bytes) | image | `256` | Parameter description capacity in bytes |
| [`params.max_name_bytes`](#paramsmax_name_bytes) | image | `-1` | Longest parameter name in bytes (-1 = derive) |
| [`params.max_parameters`](#paramsmax_parameters) | image | `-1` | Maximum declared parameters per image (-1 = derive) |
| [`params.max_string_array_len`](#paramsmax_string_array_len) | image | `-1` | String-array parameter capacity in elements (-1 = derive) |
| [`params.max_string_value_bytes`](#paramsmax_string_value_bytes) | image | `-1` | String parameter capacity in bytes (-1 = derive) |
| [`params.service_inbox_bytes`](#paramsservice_inbox_bytes) | image | `-1` | Parameter/lifecycle service inbox slot size (bytes, -1 = derive) |
| [`params.service_inbox_depth`](#paramsservice_inbox_depth) | image | `1` | Parameter/lifecycle service inbox ring depth |

### `params.events_depth`

/parameter_events publisher history depth

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.params] events_depth`
- **Or for a board:** `nros-board.toml`, `[knobs] params.events_depth`
- **Scope:** image
- **Values:** an integer from 1 to 1000
- **Default:** `1`

History depth of each node's /parameter_events publisher, read by
nros-params build.rs. Upstream's
parameter_events profile is KEEP_LAST(1000); a reliable DDS writer
reserves that history, so an RTOS image defaults to 1. Depth is not a
QoS matching criterion, so a subscriber with upstream's profile still
matches.

### `params.max_array_len`

Array parameter capacity in elements (-1 = derive)

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.params] max_array_len`
- **Or for a board:** `nros-board.toml`, `[knobs] params.max_array_len`
- **Scope:** image
- **Values:** an integer
- **Default:** `-1`

Elements a `bool_array`, `integer_array` or `double_array` parameter
can hold (nros-params build.rs). A `string_array` has its own element
bound, MAX_STRING_ARRAY_LEN.

-1 DERIVES 0 when the contract's `params:` declare none of those
types. When one is declared, state a number here; the build refuses,
naming the parameter and this knob, if nothing does. Without a
declaration the crate default of 32 stands.

### `params.max_byte_array_bytes`

Byte-array parameter capacity in bytes (-1 = derive)

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.params] max_byte_array_bytes`
- **Or for a board:** `nros-board.toml`, `[knobs] params.max_byte_array_bytes`
- **Scope:** image
- **Values:** an integer
- **Default:** `-1`

Bytes a `byte_array` parameter can hold (nros-params build.rs).

-1 DERIVES 0 when the contract's `params:` declare no byte_array.
When one is declared, state a number here; the build refuses, naming
the parameter and this knob, if nothing does. Without a declaration
the crate default of 256 stands.

### `params.max_constraints_bytes`

Parameter additional_constraints capacity in bytes

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.params] max_constraints_bytes`
- **Or for a board:** `nros-board.toml`, `[knobs] params.max_constraints_bytes`
- **Scope:** image
- **Values:** an integer from 0 to 256
- **Default:** `0`

Longest `additional_constraints` a parameter's descriptor can hold
(nros-params build.rs) -- the free text `ros2 param describe` prints
and rclc's rclc_add_parameter_description takes as its fourth
argument. Paid once per store slot whatever the slot holds.

A board fact, never derived, exactly like
`params.max_description_bytes` beside it. It has its OWN knob rather
than sharing that one, and the DEFAULT IS 0: the describe reply's
derived buffer prices CAPACITY, not use, so sharing would have cost
every image 256 bytes per parameter for a field it never sets -- 2,048
bytes on an eight-parameter image, taking its reply past
the 4,096 fallback. State a number here to use the field. Longer text
is truncated at a character boundary and logged once per parameter,
naming this knob.

### `params.max_description_bytes`

Parameter description capacity in bytes

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.params] max_description_bytes`
- **Or for a board:** `nros-board.toml`, `[knobs] params.max_description_bytes`
- **Scope:** image
- **Values:** an integer from 0 to 256
- **Default:** `256`

Longest DESCRIPTION a parameter's descriptor can hold
(nros-params build.rs). Paid once per store slot whatever the slot
holds, like the other per-slot limits.

A board fact, never derived: the contract states a
parameter's name and type, not its description. 0 is a real choice
meaning "no descriptions". A longer description is truncated at a
character boundary and logged once per parameter, naming this knob.
256 is the most an rcl_interfaces describe reply carries.

### `params.max_name_bytes`

Longest parameter name in bytes (-1 = derive)

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.params] max_name_bytes`
- **Or for a board:** `nros-board.toml`, `[knobs] params.max_name_bytes`
- **Scope:** image
- **Values:** an integer
- **Default:** `-1`

Per-slot name capacity of the parameter store (nros-params build.rs).

-1 DERIVES it from the contract's `params:` -- the longest declared
name, and never shorter than `use_sim_time`. Without a declaration
the crate default of 64 stands.

### `params.max_parameters`

Maximum declared parameters per image (-1 = derive)

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.params] max_parameters`
- **Or for a board:** `nros-board.toml`, `[knobs] params.max_parameters`
- **Scope:** image
- **Values:** an integer
- **Default:** `-1`

Static parameter-store pool size (nros-params build.rs). A node
declaring more parameters than this is refused at boot: the runtime
logs the node, the parameter and this knob, and the declaration
fails (C++ stops the boot with Full, -6). The Autoware trajectory follower
declares ~150.

-1 DERIVES it from the contract's `params:`: every
declared parameter plus one `use_sim_time` per node, which nano-ros
declares on every node. An image whose contract declares no
parameters (or declares them on only some nodes) falls through to the
crate default of 32. Stating a number here WINS.

### `params.max_string_array_len`

String-array parameter capacity in elements (-1 = derive)

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.params] max_string_array_len`
- **Or for a board:** `nros-board.toml`, `[knobs] params.max_string_array_len`
- **Scope:** image
- **Values:** an integer
- **Default:** `-1`

Elements a `string_array` parameter can hold (nros-params build.rs);
each element is bounded by MAX_STRING_VALUE_LEN. A string array is
the largest value a slot can hold (elements x string length), and
every slot is as large as the largest value, so this bound is kept
apart from MAX_ARRAY_LEN: an image with a `string` and a
`double_array` but no `string_array` pays for neither product.

-1 DERIVES 0 when the contract's `params:` declare no `string_array`.
When one is declared, state a number here; the build refuses, naming
the parameter and this knob, if nothing does. Without a declaration
the crate default of 32 stands.

### `params.max_string_value_bytes`

String parameter capacity in bytes (-1 = derive)

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.params] max_string_value_bytes`
- **Or for a board:** `nros-board.toml`, `[knobs] params.max_string_value_bytes`
- **Scope:** image
- **Values:** an integer
- **Default:** `-1`

Longest string a `string` or `string_array` parameter can hold, and
the capacity of a parameter DESCRIPTION (nros-params build.rs). Every
store slot is as large as the largest value the limits allow, so this
is paid once per slot whatever the slot holds.

-1 DERIVES 0 when the contract's `params:` declare no string, which is
what takes a scalar-only image's slot from ~8.9 KiB to 168 bytes; at 0
no parameter can carry a description either. When a node DOES declare
a string the contract cannot say how long it may be -- that is a fact
about the board -- so state a number here, and the build refuses,
naming the parameter and this knob, if nothing does. Without a
declaration the crate default of 256 stands.

### `params.service_inbox_bytes`

Parameter/lifecycle service inbox slot size (bytes, -1 = derive)

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.params] service_inbox_bytes`
- **Scope:** image
- **Values:** an integer
- **Default:** `-1`

Bytes one request slot holds in the inbox ring of each
ROS parameter service queryable (six per node) and each REP-2002
lifecycle service queryable (five per node).

-1 means DERIVE it, which is what almost every image wants: nros-node
and nros-rmw-zenoh then size the slot from the contract's declared
parameters, as the largest request a set_parameters over the
worst-declared node can produce, against the parameter store's
resolved capacities. For example, a largest set_parameters of 1015
bytes gives a 1016-byte slot (rounded to the slot alignment).

Any other value STATES the size and wins over the derivation. A stated
size smaller than the declarations can produce FAILS THE BUILD naming
this symbol, rather than dropping a well-formed request at run time.
0 is not a size and is refused: it used to be this symbol's derive
sentinel, and the readers took it literally. On XRCE the same number
is XRCE_PARAM_REQUEST_BYTES, which raises
`xrce.service_request_buffer_bytes` to fit it.

Not under NROS_RMW_ZENOH, unlike PARAMS_SERVICE_INBOX_DEPTH (whose ring
only a caller-inbox backend allocates): nros-node and the XRCE backend
read this size too, so an XRCE image must be able to state it. Under
the zenoh `if` it was undeclared there, while XRCE's own refusal told
the user to set it.
Maps to `params.service_inbox_bytes`.

### `params.service_inbox_depth`

Parameter/lifecycle service inbox ring depth

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.params] service_inbox_depth`
- **Scope:** image
- **Values:** an integer
- **Default:** `1`

Requests one parameter or lifecycle service queryable
holds before the newest is dropped.

One, because this traffic is one request and one reply from a client
that waits: ros2 param and rclcpp's SyncParametersClient block on each
call, and a node's six services are polled serially in one spin. Two
clients hitting the SAME service of the SAME node inside one spin
period is the only case depth 1 loses, and the loser sees a timeout and
retries. Raise it to 2 for an image that serves a parameter dashboard.
Must be >= 1. Maps to `params.service_inbox_depth`.

## `pubsub`

Knobs for publishers and subscriptions.

| Knob | Scope | Default | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`pubsub.qos_depth`](#pubsubqos_depth) | image | `10` | QoS history depth the arena budgets per subscription |

### `pubsub.qos_depth`

QoS history depth the arena budgets per subscription

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.pubsub] qos_depth`
- **Scope:** image
- **Values:** an integer
- **Default:** `10`

How deep a history the executor arena reserves for each pub/sub
callback slot. 10 is ROS 2's own default -- `rmw_qos_profile_default`
is KEEP_LAST(10), which is what a subscription created with no QoS
argument actually gets -- so an image that says nothing here is sized
the way ROS would size it.

STATE 1 IF YOUR SUBSCRIPTIONS ARE KEEP_LAST(1), and the saving is large
rather than marginal. The buffer shape is a step function, not a slope:
depth 1 is a TripleBuffer of 3 slots and anything deeper is an SpscRing
of depth+1, so the default budgets 11 slots where 3 would do. For
example, an image with 11 subscriptions, 4 timers and 2 service servers
measured 144,584 bytes of arena at 10, 53,504 at 1.

This is the IMAGE-WIDE number. A per-endpoint answer is derived instead
from `<stem>.contract.yaml`'s `qos.depth` when EVERY endpoint states
one; that is finer, needs no knob, and this value still wins
over it -- env > Kconfig/board > derived > default, the ladder every
derivable knob follows.

TOO SMALL IS NOT A SMALLER BUFFER. The arena is sized from this, and an
arena that does not fit halts during entity creation, before the first
spin -- so raise it, or state the depths, rather than trimming it to fit.

Knobs for the RMW layer, backend-independent.

| Knob | Scope | Default | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| [`rmw.max_backends`](#rmwmax_backends) | image | per platform | (no description yet) |
| [`rmw.max_nodes`](#rmwmax_nodes) | image | per platform | (no description yet) |

| [`rmw.subscriber_slot_bytes`](#rmwsubscriber_slot_bytes) | image | per platform | (no description yet) |
| [`rmw.subscriber_slots`](#rmwsubscriber_slots) | image | `-1` | Static subscription-handle slots (no_std targets) (-1 = derive) |

### `rmw.local_queryable`

Same-session query delivery (-1 = derive, 0 = off, 1 = on)

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.rmw] local_queryable`
- **Scope:** image
- **Values:** an integer from -1 to 1
- **Default:** `-1`

Maps to Z_FEATURE_LOCAL_QUERYABLE, zenoh-pico's same-session query
path. Every node of a Zephyr image shares ONE zenoh session, and
neither zenoh-pico nor the router sends a query back to the session
it came from. So a service client and a service server in the SAME
image never meet without this: the call goes out, no server answers,
and nothing reports it (for example, a request from one node never
reaches the server node beside it in the same image).

`-1` DERIVES it from the image's entity inventory: on when the image
declares at least one service client (an action client counts, it
opens three) AND at least one service server (an action server
counts, three queryables), off otherwise. An image with only one
side of a service pays nothing for a path it cannot use. The sibling
for topics, Z_FEATURE_LOCAL_SUBSCRIBER, is always on.

Stating 0 or 1 WINS over the derivation, as for every derivable
knob. Where the inventory cannot answer (a component that declares
nothing), the knob keeps zenoh-pico's own default, 0, and the
configure says so.

The name is the RMW's, not zenoh's, because the boot record in
nros-node carries the resolved value and its rung, and a core crate
names no backend. Only the zenoh backend consumes it.

### `rmw.max_backends`

(no description yet)

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.rmw] max_backends`
- **Or for a board:** `nros-board.toml`, `[knobs] rmw.max_backends`
- **Scope:** image
- **Values:** an integer of 0 or more
- **Default:** set per platform and board; `nros knob list --platform <p>` shows the value one platform gets, and which rung set it

### `rmw.max_nodes`

(no description yet)

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.rmw] max_nodes`
- **Or for a board:** `nros-board.toml`, `[knobs] rmw.max_nodes`
- **Scope:** image
- **Values:** an integer of 0 or more
- **Default:** set per platform and board; `nros knob list --platform <p>` shows the value one platform gets, and which rung set it

### `rmw.message_info_slots`

(no description yet)

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.rmw] message_info_slots`
- **Or for a board:** `nros-board.toml`, `[knobs] rmw.message_info_slots`
- **Scope:** image
- **Values:** an integer of 0 or more
- **Default:** set per platform and board; `nros knob list --platform <p>` shows the value one platform gets, and which rung set it

### `rmw.subscriber_slot_bytes`

(no description yet)

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.rmw] subscriber_slot_bytes`
- **Or for a board:** `nros-board.toml`, `[knobs] rmw.subscriber_slot_bytes`
- **Scope:** image
- **Values:** an integer of 0 or more
- **Default:** set per platform and board; `nros knob list --platform <p>` shows the value one platform gets, and which rung set it

### `rmw.subscriber_slots`

Static subscription-handle slots (no_std targets) (-1 = derive)

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.rmw] subscriber_slots`
- **Scope:** image
- **Values:** an integer
- **Default:** `-1`

nros-rmw-cffi keeps subscription handles in a static slot pool on
no_std targets, since there is no allocator to Box them into. The
Nth+1 create_subscription returns BAD_ALLOC and the executor surfaces
it as an opaque SubscriberCreationFailed, so this must be at least the
number of subscriptions the image creates. Pool size is this x 1024
bytes. Read by nros-rmw-cffi build.rs.

`-1` DERIVES this from the image's entity inventory
(`nano_ros_node_register(... ENTITIES ...)`). Stating a number here WINS
and suppresses the derivation, which is a fine thing to do deliberately
and a silent cost otherwise.

The derived value counts what the SESSION opens, which is not what the
author declares: a declared action server is one entity that costs three
queryables and two publishers, and an action client one subscription.
Those multipliers live beside the calls that decide them.

NOT counted, because a feature enables them and the inventory cannot see
it: the parameter (6) and lifecycle (5) service families. An image
carrying either must state this knob.

## `service`

Knobs for service servers and clients.

| Knob | Scope | Default | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`service.inbox_bytes`](#serviceinbox_bytes) | image | `-1` | Service inbox slot size (bytes, -1 = derive) |
| [`service.inbox_depth`](#serviceinbox_depth) | image | `4` | Service inbox ring depth |
| [`service.timeout_ms`](#servicetimeout_ms) | image | per platform | (no description yet) |

### `service.inbox_bytes`

Service inbox slot size (bytes, -1 = derive)

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.service] inbox_bytes`
- **Scope:** image
- **Values:** an integer
- **Default:** `-1`

Bytes one request slot holds in the inbox ring of every USER service
server (a zenoh queryable). The parameter and lifecycle services do
not share it: they bring their own ring, sized by nros-node from the
contract's declared parameters. Maps to
`service.inbox_bytes` in nros-rmw-zenoh's build script. A request
larger than this is dropped with TransportError::MessageTooLarge.

-1 means DERIVE it: the largest bound among the
`pkg/srv/Name_Request` types this image's declared service servers and
clients carry, which codegen prices and the entity inventory joins.
Any other value is yours and WINS. If NOTHING derives -- no contract,
or one request type with no static bound -- the crate falls through to
NROS_SERVICE_BUFFER_SIZE (1024), and the configure says which.

The derivation outranks the DEPRECATED alias NROS_SERVICE_BUFFER_SIZE
and nothing else: to pin a size, state THIS symbol.

Per queryable the ring costs
  `service.inbox_depth` x (`service.inbox_bytes` + 12)
plus a fixed header; a static-memory report of the image prices it
exactly.

### `service.inbox_depth`

Service inbox ring depth

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.service] inbox_depth`
- **Scope:** image
- **Values:** an integer
- **Default:** `4`

Requests one USER service server holds before the newest is dropped.
4 was chosen for the action path (a burst of queries in one read-task
batch) and every family paid it; the parameter family's own depth is
1, on its own ring. Must be >= 1. Maps to
`service.inbox_depth`.

### `service.timeout_ms`

(no description yet)

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.service] timeout_ms`

## `subscriber`

Knobs for subscriber buffers.

| Knob | Scope | Default | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`subscriber.buffer_bytes`](#subscriberbuffer_bytes) | image | `-1` | Per-subscriber static buffer size (-1 = derive) |

### `subscriber.buffer_bytes`

Per-subscriber static buffer size (-1 = derive)

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.subscriber] buffer_bytes`
- **Scope:** image
- **Values:** an integer
- **Default:** `-1`

Size of the static buffer for each subscriber slot (bytes) -- the SMALL
zenoh payload class. Maps to `subscriber.buffer_bytes` (one name: the
executor arena reads it too).

-1 means DERIVE it from this image's message-bound inventory: the
largest derived bound at or under the
small/large class split (`zenoh.subscriber_large_threshold_bytes`, 2048 by
default; it has no Kconfig row). Any other value is yours and WINS.

READ THIS BEFORE TRUSTING THE DERIVED NUMBER. The inventory holds every
type in the LINKED interface closure, not only the ones you subscribe to,
so the derived size is an UPPER BOUND: too big, never too small. For
example, an image can derive 1496 B, set by std_msgs/Float64MultiArray,
against 880 B for the largest type it actually receives -- the
difference is the price of deriving from linked types rather than from
the entities the image declares.
The configure prints which type set the number; if it is one you do not
receive, state your own value here.

If ANY type in the closure has no derived bound, NOTHING is derived and
the crate default (1024) applies -- the configure says so and names the
types. Deriving over the bounded subset would publish a maximum a real
sample can exceed, which is a SILENT drop on the C++ arena path.

### `xrce.buffer_bytes`

Per-slot static buffer size

- **Set it in:** `system.toml`, `[image.<id>.knobs.xrce] buffer_bytes`
- **Scope:** image
- **Package:** `nros_rmw_xrce`
- **Values:** an integer
- **Default:** `1024`

Size of the static buffer for each subscriber/service slot (bytes).
Maps to XRCE_BUFFER_SIZE.

This is the DEFAULT of the three per-family sizes
(`xrce.subscriber_buffer_bytes`, `xrce.service_request_buffer_bytes`,
`xrce.service_reply_buffer_bytes`), not an array size of its own. It stays the one lever that
moves every receive buffer at once; state a family option instead
when only one of them needs the room.
